newsitem.title: USA: Buba to voice concern if dlr rises more--economist.
newsitem.headline: Buba to voice concern if dlr rises more--economist.

text.p: The Bundesbank is likely to voice concern if the dollar continues to march higher against the mark, but it is unlikely to raise key interest rates in response, an economist from a leading German bank said on Monday.

"You might have a statement from the Bundesbank that it considers the market on the verge of being disorderly," said Klaus Friedrich, chief economist of Dresdner Bank. "I don't expect the Bundesbank to raise key interest rates."
The German central bank though might at some point consider raising its repurchase rate, he told reporters.

However, Friedrich said he does not expect the dollar to climb sharply against the German currency, although he added he would not be surprised if it broke through 1.80 marks. The dollar rose to a fresh 71-month high of 1.7960 marks Monday.
"I don't see a reason for the dollar to go, go, go," Friedrich said.
He put the equilibrium rate for dollar/mark at about 1.75, give or take 10 pfennigs. That is a level that the German economy can fundamentally live with.
Noting that other European currencies have weakened recently in tandem with the mark, Friedrich said the yet-to-be-launched euro may be facing its first test.
"There is a sense in the market that these currencies belong together," the economist said.

He voiced confidence that the euro will be launched on time in 1999. He said he could not rule out the possibility that Germany will be able to reduce its budget deficit to the equivalent of three percent of gross domestic product this year, although his forecast calls for a slightly higher gap.
Friedrich said the introduction of the euro may prompt Germany to carry out much-needed and long-delayed structural economic reforms. "I see the euro as a catalyst," he said.
